Why turning the key isn't what starts the car.

Kevin Trudeau uses a simple picture: if the battery isn't connected, turning the key does nothing. The key is the action, but the battery is what makes it work.

He calls this the cause behind the cause, the real source of an effect, working underneath the surface.

Kevin says that once he understood this idea, he saw results in a very different way.

What might be the hidden battery behind the results in your own life?

What you resist persists. Here is what to do instead.

Kevin Trudeau shares a simple three-step procedure for when something hard shows up in your life.

First, acknowledge it and don't deny it. Second, accept it and welcome it instead of fighting it. Third, learn the lesson and take full responsibility.

Kevin says that when you do this, it burns off and is gone.

When did resisting something only make it stick around longer for you?

#ad #karma #mindset #habits

How you talk about people when they're not there comes back to you.

Kevin Trudeau calls this rule two of the expanded golden rule: talk about people the way you wish they would talk about you.

He shares a moment in a cigar lounge when he was about to say something negative about a man. He stopped and chose to say what he liked about him instead.

Kevin says that with deliberate intent you plant good seeds that return to you many times over.

How do you talk about people when they're not in the room?

The biggest lie is always the one you tell yourself.

Kevin Trudeau says the second biggest lie is the half truth. Then he gives a simple image: the best time to plant a tree was twenty years ago, and the second best time is today.

You can't go back and plant it in the past, but you can start planting now.

Kevin applies the same idea to the good karma you create: the best time was long ago, and the second best time is today.

What is one thing you've told yourself that deserves a second look?
